name: intraday-equities-p7-pls-h02
notes: P7 shortlist cell: a feature row every 5 minute(s), a look-ahead of 2 minute(s), partial least squares, a projection-based linear model. One of nineteen cells that differ from the P1 s05 grid in exactly ONE place - the scan's estimator block (estimator, estimator_params and the purged search over it, ADR-0060). The row spacing, the look-ahead, the features, the folds, the label, the cohort, the store, the study start and the 30-minute scoring lattice are byte-for-byte the values run-p1-s05-h02-ridge.json carries, so a P7 cell is read straight against its P1 twin at the same look-ahead and only the model differs (ADR-0065). Every P7 cell also gets the SAME purged inner-holdout search on the SAME objective, which is the unfairness docs/research/p7-model-size-for-this-noise-level-*.md found: ridge and the trees were each searched, the three nets were not, so 'bigger is worse' was partly a statement about tuning effort. Scored under ADR-0067 and raised to ADR-0069's many-attempts bar - nineteen more cells raise that bar for everything, which is the price of the shortlist. Reads nothing at or after 2026-03-01.

universe.notes: The H<=20 grid variant, with the row spacing overridden to 5 minute(s) for this cell (ADR-0065). The cohort, calendar and holdout dates stay exactly the shared ones.

alpaca.notes: Split-adjusted historical SIP tape (source alpaca-sip-split, ADR-0063): AAPL's 2020 4-for-1, WMT's 2024 3-for-1 and the XLE/XLK 2-for-1s of December 2025 are all removed by the vendor, so no change of unit reads as a price move. start_ms is the study's start date, 2018-01-01 (ADR-0066) - it precedes the earliest bar any fold reads by 2y4m, and it puts XLF's 2016-09-19 XLRE spin-off, the one corporate action the vendor does NOT adjust, outside the readable window. Prices here are NOT the as-traded scale and are not comparable with any number recorded before 2026-09-03. Run from the child root.

features.notes: lookback=20 emits one-minute ret_lag columns for the last 20 minutes. Every horizon here is cross_session so none costs rows beyond a one-time warmup; see docs/research/row-loss-is-intra-session-scale-warmup-not-cross-session.md.

tradable.notes: SPY has already entered the residual features; score tradables.

scan.notes: P7 item 3, the natural step past ridge: instead of shrinking 87 coefficients toward zero, project the columns onto a handful of directions chosen for their covariance with the label, then regress on those. That is a supervised, harder shrinkage than ridge's, and the component count IS the capacity knob, so the five-point grid spans the whole model. It scales its own columns (scale: true), which nothing else in this seam does - _fit_estimator applies no scaling and a run document cannot express an sklearn Pipeline. hpo_trials is 5, not 6, because the grid has exactly five points and a sixth draw would be a repeat. Everything outside estimator/estimator_params/hpo_* is the P1 s05 cell verbatim: split val, the fold's own cuts, label_scale vol, label_residual SPY, lead_start=lead_step=lead_stop=2 (ADR-0062: lead_start is also the training label, so this cell trains and scores at 2 minute(s) and nowhere else), and score_period_ms 1800000 so only validation rows on the half-hour are judged and the Newey-West lag comes from the lattice, not the spacing (ADR-0065). The search is the P1 ridge cell's: 5 draws on a 63-day inner holdout carved out of train with a 5-day embargo, chosen on IC, the fold's own validation never read.

names.notes: All five tradables. AAPL and WMT were excluded while the tape carried unadjusted splits; the split-adjusted store (ADR-0063) removed that reason, so the cohort that builds the features and the cohort that gets SCORED are the same five again. Sits after tradable so a later run can narrow what is scored without touching what is built.

walkforward.notes: Same post-COVID folds as run-hstar-cv-postcovid.json so the two are comparable: first validation 2022-05-06, twenty 63-day steps, a real 730-day bounded training window, last validation inside the 2025-11-30 cut. objective is val_ic, NOT go_frac: counting fold-level rejections and taking the max is vote counting, which Hedges-Olkin showed is inconsistent when per-fold power is below one half (A0035). The winner here only labels a fold in the summary; the science is the per-fold sequence, which is what the block-by-block reading needs. embargo_days=5 is now larger than any label window on this grid (20 minutes), so no training row's label can reach into validation.
